CREATE VIEW v_derived_figure_check AS
SELECT
    d.extraction_id                                              AS derived_id,
    CAST(d.claimed_value AS REAL)                                 AS stored,
    CAST(b.claimed_value AS REAL)                                 AS base_value,
    CAST(e.claimed_value AS REAL)                                 AS delta_value,
    CAST(b.claimed_value AS REAL) + CAST(e.claimed_value AS REAL) AS recomputed
FROM source_value_extractions d
JOIN extraction_relations rb
  ON rb.from_extraction_id = d.extraction_id
 AND rb.relation = 'derived_from'
 AND rb.input_role = 'base'
JOIN source_value_extractions b ON b.extraction_id = rb.to_extraction_id
JOIN extraction_relations rd
  ON rd.from_extraction_id = d.extraction_id
 AND rd.relation = 'derived_from'
 AND rd.input_role = 'delta'
JOIN source_value_extractions e ON e.extraction_id = rd.to_extraction_id
WHERE d.figure_role = 'derived'
  AND d.claimed_value GLOB '*[0-9]*' AND d.claimed_value NOT GLOB '*[^0-9.eE+-]*'
  AND b.claimed_value GLOB '*[0-9]*' AND b.claimed_value NOT GLOB '*[^0-9.eE+-]*'
  AND e.claimed_value GLOB '*[0-9]*' AND e.claimed_value NOT GLOB '*[^0-9.eE+-]*'
  AND d.claimed_unit = b.claimed_unit
  AND d.claimed_unit = e.claimed_unit
CREATE VIEW v_determination_provenance AS
SELECT s.specification_id,
       s.parameter_id,
       t.canonical_en                AS parameter_name,
       s.state,
       COALESCE(s.identity_code, s.icf_code, s.needs_code) AS lens,
       l.role,
       l.exclusion_reason,
       x.extraction_id,
       x.figure_role,
       x.comparator,
       x.claimed_value,
       x.claimed_unit,
       x.claim_text,
       x.ref_id,
       e.tier,
       e.evidence_type,
       e.verification_status
  FROM specifications s
  JOIN specification_extraction_links l ON l.specification_id = s.specification_id
  JOIN source_value_extractions       x ON x.extraction_id    = l.extraction_id
  JOIN base_parameters                p ON p.parameter_id     = s.parameter_id
                                       AND p.status             = 'active'
  JOIN terms                          t ON t.term_id          = p.term_id
  LEFT JOIN evidence_sources          e ON e.ref_id           = x.ref_id
 WHERE s.retired_at IS NULL
CREATE VIEW v_scan_ledger AS
-- v_scan_ledger: one row per (source in scope) x (active parameter).
--
--   source in scope   evidence_sources with superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL. A tombstone is
--                     never read again; its replacement is.
--   active parameter  base_parameters.status = 'active'. Retired and merged parameters
--                     leave the ledger (their extractions stay, as history).
--
-- STATUS PRECEDENCE, first match wins:
--   1 EXTRACTED          a live (not retired, migration 158) non-absent extraction exists for the pair
--                        (any figure_role).
--   2 STATED-ABSENT      only live claim_type 'absent' extractions exist: the source addresses
--                        the quantity and sets nothing -- a positive statement.
--   3 READ-NOTHING-FOUND a FULL-scope reading covers the pair and found no row.
--   4 BLOCKED            no full reading covers the pair AND the source carries an obstacle
--                        processing_blocked_reason (below): the full text could not be
--                        obtained or read, so the pair is not reading debt until a full
--                        reading is recorded. Any partial / fragment / abstract reading of
--                        the pair is still named in scan_id / text_scope / method.
--   5 READ-PARTIAL       only partial / fragment / abstract readings cover it, and no
--                        obstacle stands: the full text is obtainable and unread -- debt.
--   6 NOT-READ           no reading covers it.
-- WHY THIS ORDER (it is derived from what each fact proves; 122 ranked BLOCKED above every
-- reading and 123 below every reading, both guesses): a FULL reading proves the obstacle
-- gone, since the whole text was read, so 3 outranks 4. A partial, fragment or abstract
-- reading proves nothing about the full text, so under a standing obstacle 4 outranks 5.
-- A reading COVERS a pair when it is catalogue-mode with catalogue_version >= parameter_id
-- (the parameter existed when the reading was made), or targeted at that parameter. Rows 1
-- and 2 win over readings because a row written is stronger evidence than a reading
-- recorded; 3 wins over the rest because a full reading supersedes a partial one.
--
-- THE BLOCKED CASE BELOW IS THE ONE HOME of "the text could not be obtained or read", and
-- this header is the ONE HOME of the classification of every processing_blocked_reason
-- value (evidence_sources CHECK, migration 091); each value appears here as a bare token
-- under exactly one head, and a test derives the CHECK and fails on a value this header
-- does not name. The writers and gates read this view's status, never the column. NOTHING
-- CLEARS THE COLUMN: it is the retrieval record and stays as history; the ledger alone says
-- whether a pair is still blocked.
--   obstacle to the text (BLOCKED, above):  no-full-text, paywalled, language.
--   copy of a typed fact (not an obstacle; the writers refuse it by pointer -- the judgement
--     lives in db.py _BLOCK_REASON_COPIES): no-quantified-claims -> a recorded full reading;
--     superseded -> superseded_by_ref_id.
--   pending owner question 8 of the round-3 adjudication, treated as NULL (the source owes
--     its reading): out-of-scope, tier-not-required (they say no text was unobtainable);
--     no-doi, not-indexed (migration 091's comments describe discovery -- "no resolvable
--     identifier for automated paths", "absent from the indexes the pipeline queries" --
--     not an obstacle to a text in hand, and a URL-only report admitted without a DOI can
--     be read).
--
-- scan_id / text_scope / method name the STRONGEST covering reading (full scope first,
-- then full-read before pre-screen, then the latest), so a READ-NOTHING-FOUND resting on
-- a pre-screen only is visible as such. NULL when no reading covers the pair.
WITH pairs AS (
    SELECT e.ref_id, p.parameter_id, e.processing_blocked_reason
      FROM evidence_sources e
     CROSS JOIN base_parameters p
     WHERE e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL
       AND p.status = 'active'
),
best AS (
    SELECT pr.ref_id, pr.parameter_id, pr.processing_blocked_reason,
           (SELECT s.scan_id FROM source_scans s
             WHERE s.ref_id = pr.ref_id
               AND ((s.mode = 'catalogue' AND s.catalogue_version >= pr.parameter_id)
                 OR (s.mode = 'targeted' AND s.target_parameter_id = pr.parameter_id))
             ORDER BY (s.text_scope = 'full') DESC, (s.method = 'full-read') DESC,
                      s.scan_id DESC
             LIMIT 1) AS scan_id
      FROM pairs pr
)
SELECT b.ref_id,
       b.parameter_id,
       CASE
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type <> 'absent' AND x.retired_at IS NULL) THEN 'EXTRACTED'
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type = 'absent' AND x.retired_at IS NULL) THEN 'STATED-ABSENT'
         WHEN s.text_scope = 'full' THEN 'READ-NOTHING-FOUND'
         WHEN b.processing_blocked_reason IN
              ('no-full-text', 'paywalled', 'language') THEN 'BLOCKED'
         WHEN s.scan_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'READ-PARTIAL'
         ELSE 'NOT-READ'
       END AS status,
       b.scan_id,
       s.text_scope,
       s.method
  FROM best b
  LEFT JOIN source_scans s ON s.scan_id = b.scan_id

[("CREATE VIEW v_reading_owed AS
-- v_reading_owed: the (source, parameter) pairs whose reading is owed. One row per pair of v_scan_ledger that no FULL
-- reading covers (text_scope is the strongest covering reading's; NULL when none covers) and that the ledger does not
-- read BLOCKED. A partial, fragment or abstract reading covers nothing here, as in the ledger. Written once: the verb
-- `db.py defer-reading` asks it whether a deferral is allowed and v_deferred_acts asks it whether one still stands.
SELECT ref_id, parameter_id
  FROM v_scan_ledger
 WHERE COALESCE(text_scope, '') <> 'full'
   AND status <> 'BLOCKED'",), ('CREATE VIEW v_deferred_acts AS
-- v_deferred_acts: every deferral that still STANDS, one row each, with the date it was first recorded.
--   kind                subject
--   search              the exec id, with its slug when it has one
--   mining              the mined ref_id and the slug
--   reading             the ref_id and the parameter (or the whole source)
--   adjudication        the observation id, its ref_id and its surface form
-- ref_id and parameter_id are the same facts as columns, so a writer asks "is this pair already deferred?" of this
-- view and cannot disagree with it (db.py defer-reading does). They are NULL where the kind has none. For a reading
-- they are the EFFECTIVE pair (see below), which is the pair the ledger owes.
-- deferred_at is the date the obligation was FIRST recorded (created_at), never the date a row was last written: a
-- re-deferral that reset the clock would hide an old obligation. An older search row carries only a date; every other
-- row, and any search logged now, a minute.
--
-- WHAT STANDS, per kind (a standing deferral is one nothing has since discharged):
--   search        EVERY deferred search. A search later run is a new row that names nothing it discharges, so a
--                 deferred search whose cell a later search covered still lists. Not derivable today.
--   mining        every citation_mining row whose OWN deferred_reason is set. The source's citation_mining_status is
--                 not read: it is one flag for every slug and both directions, so a pass for another slug sets it to
--                 'mined' while this row's deferral stands. `db.py log-mining --discharge-deferral` clears the row's
--                 deferred_reason, which is what ends it. A ref that resolves to no evidence_sources row (a lead
--                 anchor) is listed like any other. created_at is the ROW's.
--   reading       a deferral whose EFFECTIVE pair is still owed (v_reading_owed, the one definition). The effective
--                 source is the deferral's own, or its successor when the source is superseded (one hop); the
--                 effective parameter is the deferral's own, or the one it was merged into (one hop). A pair deferral
--                 stands iff its effective pair is owed; a whole-source deferral (NULL parameter) stands iff SOME
--                 active parameter of the effective source is owed. A retired parameter or a superseded successor
--                 leaves no ledger row, so it drops out. No date is read: a deferral can only be created while its
--                 cell is owed, and it stands for exactly as long as the cell is.
--   adjudication  an observation whose LATEST adjudication (highest adjudication_id, the rule alias and rename writers
--                 use) is DEFERRED: a later judgment of any other outcome discharges it.
SELECT 'search' AS kind,
       'exec ' || se.exec_id || COALESCE(' ' || se.slug, '') AS subject,
       se.mined_ref_id AS ref_id,
       se.parameter_id AS parameter_id,
       se.deferred_reason AS reason,
       se.created_at AS deferred_at,
       se.created_by_session AS created_by_session
  FROM search_executions se
 WHERE se.deferred_reason IS NOT NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT 'mining',
       COALESCE(cm.global_ref_id, cm.local_ref_id) || ' ' || cm.slug,
       COALESCE(cm.global_ref_id, cm.local_ref_id),
       NULL,
       cm.deferred_reason,
       cm.created_at,
       cm.created_by_session
  FROM citation_mining cm
 WHERE cm.deferred_reason IS NOT NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT 'reading',
       d.eff_ref || ' ' || COALESCE('parameter ' || d.eff_param, 'whole source')
         || CASE WHEN d.eff_ref <> d.ref_id OR d.eff_param IS NOT d.parameter_id
                 THEN ' (recorded for ' || d.ref_id || COALESCE(' parameter ' || d.parameter_id, ' whole source') || ')'
                 ELSE '' END,
       d.eff_ref,
       d.eff_param,
       d.reason,
       d.created_at,
       d.created_by_session
  FROM (SELECT r.*,
               COALESCE(e.superseded_by_ref_id, r.ref_id) AS eff_ref,
               CASE WHEN p.status = 'merged' THEN p.merged_into ELSE r.parameter_id END AS eff_param
          FROM reading_deferrals r
          JOIN evidence_sources e ON e.ref_id = r.ref_id
          LEFT JOIN base_parameters p ON p.parameter_id = r.parameter_id) d
 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_reading_owed o
                WHERE o.ref_id = d.eff_ref AND (d.parameter_id IS NULL OR o.parameter_id = d.eff_param))
UNION ALL
SELECT 'adjudication',
       'observation ' || o.observation_id || ' ' || o.ref_id || ' ' || o.surface_form,
       o.ref_id,
       NULL,
       a.rationale,
       a.created_at,
       a.created_by_session
  FROM term_adjudications a
  JOIN observed_terms o ON o.observation_id = a.observation_id
 WHERE a.outcome = 'DEFERRED'
   AND a.adjudication_id = (SELECT MAX(b.adjudication_id) FROM term_adjudications b
                             WHERE b.observation_id = a.observation_id)',)]

def repoint_extraction_relation(from_extraction: int, relation: str,
                                to_extraction: int, session: str,
                                dry_run: bool = False, old_label: str = None):
    """Turn an existing LABEL edge into a real ROW pointer.

    How an 'ADAAG' `to_label` edge becomes a real `to_extraction_id` pointer once
    ADA §405 is itself admitted and extracted: NULL the label and kind, point the
    edge at the new row, and ledger the old label into `notes` rather than losing
    it -- the append discipline `amend-search`/`amend-source` already use, applied
    to a column instead of a whole row.
    """
    with dbcore.connect(dry_run) as conn:
        if to_extraction == from_extraction:
            raise Refusal(
                f"--repoint: --to-extraction {to_extraction} is the same row this "
                f"edge is FROM. A figure cannot be its own comparator.")
        if not dbcore.exists(conn, "source_value_extractions",
                             "extraction_id", to_extraction):
            raise Refusal(
                f"--repoint: --to-extraction {to_extraction}: no such extraction. "
                f"Admit and extract the standard before repointing onto it.")
        if relation == "confirms":
            _refuse_live_confirmation(conn, "--repoint", to_extraction)
        q = ("SELECT relation_id, to_label FROM extraction_relations "
             "WHERE from_extraction_id=? AND relation=? AND to_extraction_id IS NULL")
        params = [from_extraction, relation]
        if old_label:
            q += " AND to_label=?"
            params.append(old_label)
        candidates = conn.execute(q, params).fetchall()
        if not candidates:
            raise Refusal(
                f"--repoint: no LABEL edge found for extraction {from_extraction}, "
                f"relation {relation!r}"
                + (f", label {old_label!r}" if old_label else "") +
                ". Nothing to repoint -- write the edge first with relate-extraction, "
                "or check --from/--relation/--old-label.")
        if len(candidates) > 1:
            raise Refusal(
                f"--repoint: {len(candidates)} label edges match extraction "
                f"{from_extraction}, relation {relation!r} -- "
                f"{[c['to_label'] for c in candidates]}. Disambiguate with "
                f"--old-label.")
        rel_id, old_label_val = candidates[0]["relation_id"], candidates[0]["to_label"]
        dup = conn.execute(
            "SELECT relation_id FROM extraction_relations WHERE from_extraction_id=? "
            "AND relation=? AND to_extraction_id=?",
            (from_extraction, relation, to_extraction)).fetchone()
        if dup:
            raise Refusal(
                f"--repoint: extraction {from_extraction} already carries a "
                f"{relation!r} edge to extraction {to_extraction} (relation_id "
                f"{dup[0]}). Repointing would collide with it -- nothing written.")
        existing_notes = conn.execute(
            "SELECT notes FROM extraction_relations WHERE relation_id=?",
            (rel_id,)).fetchone()["notes"]
        stamp = dbcore.now()
        marker = (f" || {stamp[:10]} repointed: to_label {old_label_val!r} -> "
                  f"to_extraction_id {to_extraction}")
        merged = ((existing_notes or "").rstrip() + marker).strip()
        conn.execute(
            "UPDATE extraction_relations SET to_extraction_id=?, to_label=NULL, "
            "to_kind=NULL, notes=? WHERE relation_id=?",
            (to_extraction, merged, rel_id))
    return {"relation_id": rel_id, "repointed_from_label": old_label_val,
            "to_extraction_id": to_extraction, "dry_run": dry_run}

    the branches from it and `sha()` hashes it, so an edge filed after a determination moves the
    sha instead of silently changing what the engine would answer."""

    # withdrawn condition figure does not make the claim unconditioned, so it stays a branch (K01 reads the same set).
    return sorted({r[0] for r in conn.execute(

record("T078", "the T-078 section ran to its end", False, f"{exc.__class__.__name__}: {exc}")
    # ── T-078 repair: every reader that filters a retired figure, each on a seeded figure, and the refusals the
    # adversarial pass found missing. Fixtures are TASK-FIXTURE rows written by SQL on the copy (the readers are under
    # test, not the writers); every id, code and expected value is read from the copy.
    try:
        import assess_cell as _t78r_engine                              # noqa: E402
        WHY = "TASK-FIXTURE T078R"
        PR = q("SELECT parameter_id FROM base_parameters WHERE status='active' ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 1")[0][0]
        OUT_CODE = q("SELECT identity_code FROM base_taxonomy_identity WHERE identity_code <> ? AND identity_code NOT IN "
                     "(SELECT identity_code FROM base_taxonomy_identity WHERE parent_code = ?) ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 1", POP, POP)[0][0]

        def fresh(read=True):
            r = next_ref()
            add_source(r, title=f"{WHY} source {r}")
            if read:
                readable(r)
            return r

        def seed(ref, pid=None, code=None, **kw):
            row = dict(ref_id=ref, parameter_id=pid or PR, claim_type="numerical", claimed_value="1", claimed_unit="mm",
                       claim_text=f"{WHY} 1 mm", figure_role="claim", comparator=">=", extraction_method="full-read",
                       created_at="t", created_by_session=S, updated_at="t", updated_by_session=S)
            row.update(kw)
            c = sqlite3.connect(DB)
            try:
                x = c.execute(f"INSERT INTO source_value_extractions ({','.join(row)}) VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(row))})",
                              list(row.values())).lastrowid
                c.execute("INSERT INTO extraction_lens_links (extraction_id, identity_code, basis, created_at, "
                          "created_by_session, updated_at, updated_by_session) VALUES (?, ?, 'carried', 't', ?, 't', ?)",
                          (x, code or POP, S, S))
                c.commit()
            finally:
                c.close()
            return x

        def edge(frm, rel, to, role=None):
            w("INSERT INTO extraction_relations (from_extraction_id, relation, to_extraction_id, stated, input_role, quote, "
              "created_at, created_by_session) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'named', ?, ?, 't', ?)", frm, rel, to, role, WHY, S)

        def retire(x):
            return db.retire_extraction(x, WHY, S)

        def ro():
            c = sqlite3.connect(DB)
            c.row_factory = None
            return c

        def sub(*cmd):
            cp = subprocess.run([sys.executable, *cmd], env=dict(os.environ, GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH=DB), capture_output=True,
                                text=True, cwd=str(REPO))
            return cp.stdout + cp.stderr

        LENS = {"identity_code": POP}
        RA = fresh()

        # R01 gather_confirmers: a finding of one source confirms a claim of another; the claim is retired.

        c = ro(); b1 = RC in {r["ref_id"] for r in _t78r_engine.gather_confirmers(c, PR, LENS)}; c.close()

        record("T078-23", "amend-extraction refuses each retirement column (set only by retire-extraction)",

                                             "extraction_method": "full-read"}, S,
                      relations=[{"relation": "condition_on", "to_extraction": d24, "stated": "named", "quote": WHY}],

        n_live = q("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM extraction_lens_links WHERE extraction_id=? AND retired_at IS NULL", d24)[0][0]

        record("T078-27", "add-lens-link refuses a retired figure, and retire-lens-link still refuses a retired figure's last "
               "live link (counted on the link table, not the view)",
               r27a and "was retired" in r27a and n_live == 1 and r27b and "last live link" in r27b, (r27a, r27b))
        reasons = sorted(dbcore.check_values(ro(), "extraction_follow_ups", "reason"))
        r28 = [refusal(db.raise_follow_up, d24, r, WHY, S) for r in reasons]
        w("INSERT INTO extraction_follow_ups (extraction_id, reason, warrant, raised_at, raised_by_session) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 't', ?)",

        import yaml                                                     # noqa: E402
        ob = next(s_["sql"] for s_ in yaml.safe_load((REPO / "governance" / "owner-browser.yaml").read_text())["queue"]
                  if s_["id"] == "open_follow_ups")
        shown = [r[1] for r in q(ob)]
        audit = sub("scripts/audit/extraction_follow_up_audit.py")
        record("T078-28", "raise-follow-up refuses a retired figure; the owner browser's open_follow_ups and "
               "extraction_follow_up_audit do not list a follow-up on one",
               all(m and "was retired" in m for m in r28) and not any(f"extraction {d24}:" in l for l in shown)
               and not re.search(rf"\b{d24}\b.*{WHY}", audit), (r28, audit[-200:]))
        live2 = seed(RA, claimed_value="40")
        blank = [refusal(db.retire_extraction, live2, rs, S) for rs in (" ​", "\t\n", "⁠ ﻿")]
        raws = {}
        for name, sql_, args in (
                ("reason of NBSP and ZWSP", "UPDATE source_value_extractions SET retired_at=?, retired_by_session=?, "
                 "retirement_reason=? WHERE extraction_id=?", (dbcore.now(), S, " ​", live2)),
                ("session of a tab and a newline", "UPDATE source_value_extractions SET retired_at=?, retired_by_session=?, "
                 "retirement_reason=? WHERE extraction_id=?", (dbcore.now(), "\t\n", WHY, live2)),
                ("retired_at not a date", "UPDATE source_value_extractions SET retired_at=?, retired_by_session=?, "
                 "retirement_reason=? WHERE extraction_id=?", ("not a date", S, WHY, live2)),
                ("a retired row's reason rewritten", "UPDATE source_value_extractions SET retirement_reason=? "
                 "WHERE extraction_id=?", ("another reason", d24)),
                ("a retired row's session rewritten", "UPDATE source_value_extractions SET retired_by_session=? "
                 "WHERE extraction_id=?", ("another session", d24)),
                ("the legitimate shape", "UPDATE source_value_extractions SET retired_at=?, retired_by_session=?, "
                 "retirement_reason=? WHERE extraction_id=?", (dbcore.now(), S, WHY, live2))):
            try:

               "rewrite of a retired row; the legitimate shape passes",
               all(m and "--reason is required" in m for m in blank) and raws.pop("the legitimate shape") is None

        mig = (REPO / "scripts" / "migrations" / "159_figure_retirement_holes.sql").read_text()

        zw = ",".join(str(ord(ch)) for ch in dbcore.ZERO_WIDTH)

input.message:
**The owner's execution condition still does not hold at cd778176.** Three sanctioned verbs write a live row onto a retired figure, two readers surface it as live or owed, and one unfiltered reader dead-ends a legitimate correction. All probes ran on copies in my own temp directory (now deleted); `data/guidebook.db` is unchanged (git blob 2974ed40e35a).

**1. HIGH — writers that bypass `_refuse_retired_figure`** (session `session_task-probe`, figures 11, 15, 46 retired on a copy):
- `relate-extraction --repoint --from 20 --relation audited_against --to-extraction 15` wrote relation 17 onto retired 15; `--from 14 --relation tested_at --to-extraction 46` wrote relation 10 onto retired 46. The executor's "repoint has no guard" is confirmed, and it is a hole, not a note.
- `add-connection --extraction 15` wrote CON-0001; `db.py connections --status PENDING` lists `extraction 15` as a live target.
- `request-translation --source-table source_value_extractions --source-row-id 15` created translation 1; `db.py translations --due-at synthesis` lists it as owed work.
- `skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md:311` ("the row stays and every reader drops it") is false.

**2. HIGH — walk dead-end (W).** `amend-extraction --field comparator` on base 187 is refused because retired derived figure 228 still counts as a user. The refusal says "Retire the derived row(s) first, amend, and derive again", and that is exactly what I had done. The `_used` query in `amend_extraction` (`relation='derived_from'`, no join to the live figure) is the unfiltered reader.

**3. MEDIUM — retire leaves live row edges onto the retired figure.** Retiring 46 succeeded while live 47 holds `tested_at -> 46`. `_row_only_relations()` covers only `condition_on` and `derived_from`; `tested_at`, `confirms`, `exceeds`, `audited_against` and `insufficient` edges with a row referent are not refused. I found no reader of those row edges other than `gather_confirmers`, which filters.

**4. MEDIUM — trigger and blank-guard holes (raw SQL on a copy).**
- Accepted `retired_at`: `'9999-99-99 99:99'`, `'1900-01-01 00:00'`, and a BLOB `b'2026-11-19 10:00'`.
- Accepted as a reason by the trigger: U+180E, U+00AD, U+2800, U+3164, U+200E, U+2063. The verb also accepted the five of these I tried (all but U+200E).
- U+001F: the verb refuses it and the trigger accepts it, so the comment "Blank as migration 159's triggers read it" is false.
- `retired_by_session='not-a-session'` is accepted.
- A raw `UPDATE claimed_value` or `parameter_id` on a retired row is accepted.
- `INSERT OR REPLACE` un-retires, as recorded.
- Held: `UPDATE OR REPLACE` / `OR IGNORE`, the multi-column clear, a reason rewrite, and a born-retired INSERT with a bad date or zero-width reason are all refused. NBSP+letter passes, legitimately.

**5. MEDIUM — tests.** 44 mutants over 8 variant runs; baseline 330/330; every one of T078-07..30 went red at least once. Six survivors:
- dropping `trg_sve_retirement_shape_insert` entirely (T078-29 exercises UPDATE only);
- the finality trigger's `NEW.retired_at IS NOT OLD.retired_at` conjunct (330/330 green, so re-stamping a retired row is untested);
- the second `retired_at` filter site in `v_unregistered_roots`;
- the second site in `v_root_id_conflicts`;
- `f.retired_at IS NULL` in the lean query (release after the leaning figure retires is untested);
- `_row_only_relations` parse failure returning `()`.

The executor's T078-24 statement is wrong. It goes red with the derived-input refusal alone removed, and stays green with the edge-writer loop alone removed.
